verdicts.defect: The screen does not empty afterwards, and it cannot, because it counts against a different point from the one it discards to. The file list is `changedFiles`, measured from $BARN_BASE (refs/barn/published/oci, then refs/barn/published/local, then HEAD), while discardChanges() puts the working tree back to HEAD. On w3rc, which has a baseline ref two commits behind HEAD, the list still showed the same three files after the discard, the action bar still said '3 of 3 files will be kept' and the badge still read Unsaved - so a user is told 'this cannot be undone', it is done, and nothing on the screen changes. Also worth naming: two of those three files were only different from the baseline because of commits, and 'Discard all' cannot touch a commit, so the button's own label over-promises on any extension that has ever been published or handed over. On base, which has no baseline ref, baseline resolves to HEAD and the two readings agree, which is why this did not show up before.

Every hunk carries a strip, and it quotes the prompt when one exists. With a completed turn on w3rc (a commit carrying a Barn-Turn trailer plus its record in /app/.barn/provenance.jsonl), /barn/review/w3rc/working rendered under the hunk: 'Prompt 1 of 1 | w3rc audit prompt: colour the greeting so a pressure event stands out | 3 lines . 1 minute ago | See the conversation', with '1 prompt behind this change' above the diff. The numbering is across the whole change (turnOrder), and the hover text explains how the lines were attributed ('resolved by blaming each line to the commit the turn ended in'). The matching works despite the report being -U0 and the display -U3: the report's hunk was 47-49 and the displayed hunk started at 44, and hunkProvenance matches on overlap. On base, where the pod's claude is signed out and no turn has ever ended, the strip is the honest empty state - 'No prompt recorded for any of this change's 46 lines' above the diff and '10 lines changed in the pod, no prompt recorded' on each hunk - and it never attributes those lines to a nearest turn; the hover says so outright ('The nearest prompt is not the answer, so none is named').

The chip is real and clickable with four states (checking / 'PR #N open' / 'No open PR for <branch>' / 'No GitHub token'). Separately worth flagging for whoever does get a token in: checkPullRequest() searches for a PR whose head is listBranches().current, but a packet's branch (barn/<ext>/<n>) is created with `git branch -f` and never checked out, so the branch the hand-over actually pushes is not the one the chip looks for.

There is now exactly one hard refusal in the product and it sits at the distribution boundary. distributeExtension() opens with assertGateOpen(); nothing else can reach a distribution, and the two other ways out of the pod (publishExtension for the local load, handOverForReview for the GitHub push) are deliberately ungated. It is reachable from screen 07 now: I drove the publish dialog on /barn/editor/w3rc through eight hand-written review records and read what it said each time. With no sign-offs: 'Packet 1 is waiting on both sign-offs' and the OCI and repository rows had no checkbox. Code only: 'The outcome sign-off on packet 1 is still outstanding.' Both by the same person: 'Both sign-offs on packet 1 carry the same person, Default Admin...' Two different people: chip 'Both sign-offs in', 'Packet 1 is signed off by Default Admin for the code and Other Person for the outcome.' Walking 01, 02, 10, 03, 04, 05, 12 and 13 beforehand asked for no approval anywhere. Worth knowing: the OCI push itself does not exist and the row says so ('Not built. Pushing to an OCI registry means building a Helm chart from the extension and pushing it with a registry client, and this Studio has neither in the pod and no registry configured'); the performable half of the same boundary is the 'Put the reviewed packet on the repository' row, and that one is also unavailable here because no GitHub token or repository is configured.

Created w3rc from screen 02, agreed its brief on screen 10, watched it in the workspace on screen 03, opened its diff on screen 04 and screen 12, opened its files, and read its verification on screen 13 - no approval dialog, no pending-review banner and no disabled control at any point. The publish dialog states the rule itself: the 'Load into this Rancher' and 'Push the source to GitHub' rows both carry 'No sign-off' and are tickable, and the note under the sign-offs reads 'Two people answer two questions, and only leaving the gate ... asks for them. Loading this into a Rancher to try it, or handing it over on GitHub to ask for a review, needs nobody.' The settings page's sign-off matrix cannot override this: policyNote() says out loud that a 'required' value on the dev-load row is 'recorded and not obeyed'.

Both halves can now be given and the gate refuses every incomplete combination. I gave the code half through screen 12's Approve (record: signoffs.code, principal local://user-btc48, sha cbb6995...) and the outcome half through screen 13's 'Sign off on the outcome' (record: signoffs.outcome, written by signOutcome(), which is now wired - verification.vue line 1074). Screen 13 refused the button until every criterion was answered ('2 criteria have not been looked at yet'). Then on screen 07: code approved and outcome missing -> 'The code review is signed off by Default Admin. The outcome sign-off on packet 1 is still outstanding', row not tickable, Publish disabled; outcome approved and code missing -> 'Packet 1 is waiting on both sign-offs', same refusal; both in from two different principals -> chip 'Both sign-offs in' and the dialog listed both with signer and time ('Code review | Is it safe? | Default Admin . approved just now', 'Outcome sign-off | Does it do the job? | Other Person . approved just now'). The last step of the design's script - the publish then proceeding - could not be run, because no GitHub token or repository is configured so no distribution destination is performable at all.

The two sign-offs are separate acts with separate records and the product refuses one person giving both. signCodeReview and signOutcome write independent entries carrying the Rancher principal from currentSigner(); on w3rc I produced both through the real screens and got two entries with distinct timestamps (code 17:02:16, outcome 17:07:09) that did not affect each other - approving the code left the outcome dot empty and signing the outcome left the code entry alone. The role split is enforced rather than described: signOutcome() reads the brief's '## Who asked' section and refuses anybody else, and screen 02 now writes that section at creation ('## Who asked / local://user-btc48 - Default Admin, on 2026-08-23' in w3rc's BRIEF.md), so screen 13 said 'The brief records you as the person who asked for this, so the outcome sign-off is yours to give.' With both entries carrying the same principal the gate refuses: 'Both sign-offs on packet 1 carry the same person, Default Admin. The two questions are "is it safe?" and "does it work?", and they are two sign-offs precisely because one person answering both is one opinion recorded twice.' With two different principals it opens. Nothing checks that the code reviewer is a developer, and the product does not claim to.

The hand-over is built to produce the PR and the record is written, but nothing can read it back to a reviewer and no PR can be made here. handOverForReview() assembles the packet, pushes branch barn/<ext>/<n>, opens the pull request and stores {branch, sha, base, pr, prError, pushError} in the review record; the GitHub dialog now describes exactly that ('assembles the work into a packet, pushes that packet to a branch of its own (barn/w3rc/3) in that repository, and opens a pull request against the default branch. Nothing is merged and nothing is written to main'), so the stale 'pushes straight to main' copy is gone.
verdicts.defect: Two gaps. (1) Screen 12's PR chip cannot find the PR the hand-over makes: checkPullRequest() searches for an open PR whose head is listBranches().current, but a packet's branch is created with `git branch -f` and never checked out, so the branch it searches for is never the packet's. The only reader of packets[n].pr in the product is PublishModal's gatePacketPr(), which is on screen 07, not on the review surface. (2) Unverifiable end to end in this environment: the barn-settings Secret holds no GitHub token and no repository is remembered, so the hand-over refuses before it reaches GitHub and no queue entry can be backed by a PR.

verdicts.evidence: The 'assembled at the push' half is right: assemblePacket() allocates refs/barn/packets/<n>, attaches the blame-resolved provenance index as a git note and creates branch barn/<ext>/<n>, and its only caller is handOverForReview(). What accumulates in the background is real too - /app/.barn/provenance.jsonl gains a record on every prompt the Studio sends, with the screen and the principal on it - and the queue now reads packets: distributionGate() and sinceLastLook() are called per row and the row for a change with no packet says 'Never handed over, so nobody has been asked to review it. It is still the author's own working tree.'
verdicts.defect: A dirty working tree still puts an extension in the review queue. base and w3rc have both never been handed over, and /barn/review counted 'Waiting on you 2' with both of them listed - the row explains the state in words but it is still a row in somebody's queue, so 'work for several build cycles without publishing and confirm nothing appears in the review queue' does not hold. review-queue.vue's load() enumerates every extension and enriches it, rather than enumerating packets.

verdicts.evidence: Made an intermediate change and superseded it before the review: in w3rc's pod I committed 'w3rc intermediate: add transient file' creating w3rc-transient.txt, then committed 'w3rc intermediate: remove transient file' deleting it. The baseline ref refs/barn/published/local sat two commits further back. /barn/review/w3rc/working then listed BRIEF.md, pages/Home.vue and verify-w3rc-approve.txt and did not mention w3rc-transient.txt anywhere on the page - the net difference from the baseline, with the intermediate state collapsed out. The mechanism is BASELINE_SH in extensions.ts, which resolves refs/barn/published/oci, then refs/barn/published/local, then HEAD, and every diff on screens 04, 05 and 12 goes through it. Worth knowing: base has no baseline ref at all, so its baseline falls back to HEAD and it is measuring from the last commit rather than from a published version - and no screen says which point it measured from (baselineRef()'s sentence is only consumed by components/BuildFailure.vue).

Detection works and is honest about what it is. I put two non-goals in w3rc's brief ('- No alerting', '- No w3rcscopecreep widget') and then added a line to pages/Home.vue mentioning one of them. Screen 13's Scope card went from 'The brief does not say what this was deliberately not doing' to 'This change adds lines that mention what the brief said it was deliberately not doing. A word match is not proof of anything - it is a place to look.' and listed the hits with their files: 'w3rcscopecreep - pages/Home.vue' and 'widget - pages/Home.vue'.
verdicts.defect: Neither resolution the design asks for exists. The drifted branch of the Scope card renders a warning banner and a list of term/file rows and nothing else - there is no 'accept it into the brief' control that would add the work to the brief, and no 'take it out' control that would revert it. The check is also a term match over added lines rather than a comparison of the build against the brief, so work that is outside the brief but does not reuse a non-goal's words is not flagged at all.

verdicts.evidence: Both halves work and I saw the join. Capture: pressing 'Agree and start building' on w3rc's brief put a record in the pod's /app/.barn/provenance.jsonl carrying the prompt, screen and principal - {"kind":"prompt","turn":"tmt61m5036hlol","prompt":"Read BRIEF.md in this package...","screen":"workspace","principal":"local://user-btc48","who":"Default Admin"} - so authoring provenance is captured with the person attached. Survival: with a completed turn on record (a commit carrying a Barn-Turn trailer plus its turn record), `node /seed/barn-provenance.mjs report` resolved the hunk by blame and screen 12 rendered it per hunk: 'Prompt 1 of 1 / w3rc audit prompt: colour the greeting so a pressure event stands out / 3 lines . 1 minute ago / See the conversation', with the change-wide summary '1 prompt behind this change'. The brief travels too: screen 12's left column renders w3rc's BRIEF.md as the packet - what this is for, who asked, the problem, what changes, where it appears, and its criteria. Caveat worth recording: the pod's claude is signed out, so no turn ever ends by itself (the Stop hook never runs) and every real hunk reads 'N lines changed in the pod, no prompt recorded'. I had to write the turn record and the trailer commit by hand to exercise the join; everything downstream of that - the report, the overlap match between the -U0 report and the -U3 display, and the strip - is the product's own.

The per-reviewer half is real and persists. markLook() now runs on every screen-12 load: barn-review-w3rc gained looks.pa5g3hz = {principal: local://user-btc48, name: Default Admin, packet: 1, sha: 4926d49, at: ...}, keyed by a hash of my principal rather than to the extension. After a second packet was handed over, reloading /barn/review/w3rc/working showed '1 change landed since you last looked at packet 1.' and the queue reads the same sinceLastLook() per row.
verdicts.defect: The second half of the promise does not exist: there is no way to filter the diff to what landed since. The banner says so itself ('The diff below is still the whole change rather than only the newer part of it: narrowing it needs a diff taken against the commit you last read, and nothing in the Studio takes one against an arbitrary commit yet'), and arriving from the queue's link with ?scope=since produces a warning banner naming the commit it would have measured from instead of a narrowed diff. Every diff in extensions.ts is pinned to $BARN_BASE, so the missing piece is a diff function that takes an arbitrary base.

verdicts.evidence: Both amber routes end in the same workspace. Changes requested: screen 12's Request changes on w3rc recorded the refusal and routed to /dashboard/barn/editor/w3rc?tab=terminal, and the reviewer's sentence was in that pod's assistant pane when I read it; the comment composer's 'Send to the assistant' does the same via /barn/editor/base?tab=terminal&comment=<id>; screen 13's per-criterion 'Send this back to the assistant' uses the same askAssistant transport. Build failure: screen 08's controls are 'Ask the assistant to explain this', 'Ask the assistant to fix it', 'Show me pages/NodeHealth.vue', 'Roll back to the snapshot ...' and 'Undo the last change' - all of which act on the same pod and return to the same workspace rather than opening a separate remediation surface or leaving the product.

Seeded barn.publish.failure and opened /barn/extensions/base/build-failed. There is a way back and the screen names it, but it is not the guaranteed one the design asks for: it offered 'Roll back to the snapshot "before overwriting w3-files-conflict.txt"' - a snapshot somebody else happened to take by hand 5 minutes earlier, with '4 changed files since' - and the note under it says outright 'What it rolls back to is only as good as the point above: nothing takes a snapshot automatically when a build succeeds yet, so this is the nearest point that exists rather than a guaranteed last working build.' findWayBack() falls back through last-working-build, baseline ref, newest hand-made snapshot, then HEAD, and only the first is actually a build that worked.
verdicts.defect: The design's guarantee needs a snapshot taken before every change, and nothing takes one. editor.vue's publishTo() calls recordWorkingBuild() only after a successful LOCAL publish, and that record lives in the browser's own storage, so on a fresh browser, on an extension nobody has locally published, or on the first failing build there is no working-build point at all. The screen is honest about it, which is right, but the promise ('every build is snapshotted so a failure always has a state to roll back to') does not hold. I did not click Roll back: it would have thrown away four other verifiers' work in the shared base pod.

verdicts.evidence: Drove the whole loop and read the far end. Screen 12's comment composer: typed 'w3rc SEND probe 1787503892 please rename nothing' on product.ts line 26, pressed 'Send to the assistant'; the comment was recorded in barn-review-base with my principal and time, the route became /barn/editor/base?tab=terminal&comment=<id>, editor.vue read the id back with readComment() and the pod's mc-editor tmux pane then held 'A reviewer looked at this change and asked for something. It is about product.ts around line 26. Their words: w3rc SEND probe 1787503892 please rename nothing. Make that change in the working tree and explain what you did.' The record was then stamped sentAt/sentHow='sent', and 'Just record it' leaves it unsent and the thread says so, so delivery is reported rather than assumed. Screen 12's Request changes does the same with its note, and screen 13's per-criterion 'Send this back to the assistant' is the same transport, so a rejection from either reviewer lands in the same place. Two honest gaps: the reviewer's sentence goes straight into the live session rather than arriving staged for the author to approve before it is sent, so 'the author still approves it' is only true of the answer and not of the instruction; and the composer's hint says so plainly rather than pretending otherwise.

Created the w3rc extension from screen 02 (description, outcome, name, 'Draft the brief') and the router went straight to /dashboard/barn/extensions/w3rc/brief - screen 10 - with the masthead 'BRIEF . STEP 1 OF 2 BEFORE ANY CODE IS WRITTEN'. The brief was already on disk in the pod at that point (BRIEF.md holding what I typed plus '## Who asked'), and pressing 'Agree and start building' routed on to /dashboard/barn/editor/w3rc - the workspace - and handed the brief to the assistant as the session's first instruction. Screen 04 by contrast is skippable: nothing routes through it, and I published-dialogued and reviewed from the workspace without visiting it. Worth knowing: screen 10 also offers 'Skip the brief', so the stage is on the path but not compulsory - though skipping now loses nothing, because the brief is written at creation rather than by that screen.

Wrote two distinctive criteria into w3rc's BRIEF.md under '## How we will know it worked' ('w3rc criterion one: the tab appears without a reload', 'w3rc criterion two: it says why when metrics are absent'). Screen 13 then listed exactly those two, in order, with Yes/No/Can't tell and a 'Show me' that drives the running preview to the criterion's route. Answering both Yes took the counter to 2/2 and enabled 'Sign off on the outcome'; signing wrote the verdicts back into the same file - '- **Met** at `/home`: w3rc criterion one: the tab appears without a reload' - so the evidence route is captured against the criterion. Screen 12 shows the same items read-only, and base's four criteria appear there with their captured/not-measured states.

base's pod has six files changed in its working tree and its dev-server preview renders them (screen 12's 'Rendered result' panel reported 'Loaded . just now' against http:barn-base-extension:8005/proxy), yet nothing named base exists in uiplugins.catalog.cattle.io - the only two are barn and nodehealth. Every Studio surface says the same thing rather than blurring it: screen 12's masthead reads 'base . not published yet', screen 04's action bar reads 'These changes are running in your preview only', screen 01's row reads 'local (preview)' under Running on, and the publish dialog separates 'Load into this Rancher' (which does reach everybody signed in here) from the preview. Publishing stays a separate deliberate act behind its own confirmation.

Opened the row menu for nodehealth on /barn/extensions - the one extension that is actually installed (Running on 'catalog . v0.1.0'). The menu offers 'Remove the local install' enabled and annotated with the version it would take off ('v0.1.0'); on the rows that are not installed the same item is disabled with the note 'not installed'. It is wired to removeLocalInstall(), which deletes the UIPlugin and reports 'is no longer loaded by this Rancher. The extension itself is untouched.' I did not press it: nodehealth belongs to another verifier's fixture and the brief forbids publishing, and the promise as written is that the row offers the reversal.

The two surfaces do agree, because they read the same thing: detectPermission() reads the pod's claude-session.sh, so screen 03's strip chip says 'Edits apply without asking' (hover: 'The assistant runs with --dangerously-skip-permissions in this pod') and screen 09's card says the same in longer words and marks that level 'In force'. Settings is also now a real page with all four concerns on it: 'What needs sign-off', 'GitHub connection', 'What the assistant may do without asking', 'Where previews run', 'Who can use Studio', 'What is sent to the model'.
verdicts.defect: Neither half of the promise's test can be met. (1) The permission mode is not a control anywhere - the settings card is explicit: 'Not settable, and not per user... these three are drawn as what they are: a statement of the level in force, not a choice.' So it cannot be changed in one place and seen in the other, and the design's 'the permission mode as a real control' on screen 03 does not exist either. (2) A second surface still edits the GitHub token: components/EditorSettingsModal.vue stores and removes it and is opened from screens 02, 03 and 12 (I opened it from screen 12 by clicking the 'No GitHub token' chip). It shares studio-settings.ts with the page so the two cannot disagree, and it deliberately offers only the credential, but the design's caption has screen 09 replacing the token modal outright.

verdicts.evidence: Screen 01's list is a bespoke component, not the Clusters page pattern. The element behind .studio-home__table is a DIV grid, there is no .sortable-table anywhere on the page, and grepping pkg/barn for 'SortableTable' or 'ResourceTable' returns nothing. Its headers (State, Name, Source, Running on, Last change) reproduce the pattern by hand.
verdicts.defect: The Studio is built almost entirely on its own primitives: components/ui holds SBadge, SBanner, SButton, SCard, SChip, SEmpty, SField, SIcon, SLabel, SMenu, SModal, SPanel, SRow, STabs, SToolbar, and every one of the ten screens is drawn with those. The only Rancher components imported anywhere in pkg/barn are AppModal, LabeledSelect and AsyncButton, and only in four of the older components (NewExtensionModal, PublishStatus, ExtensionSelect, ExtensionFiles). So Banner, Card, Tabbed and SortableTable are all reimplementations, and screen 01 in particular is a hand-rolled table rather than the SortableTable the rationale names.

verdicts.evidence: Re-checked all five on a freshly created extension and on base, and the two regressions from last time are gone. CLI: the workspace's Terminal tab is the pod's live tmux session (I read my own prompts back out of it with `tmux capture-pane -t mc-editor`), and the raw output is one click from the activity stream - [data-testid=barn-open-raw-output] labelled 'Open the raw output / the terminal is still here'. FILES: the Files tab lists the tree and the commit history (on a brand-new w3rc: 'd3cd0d4 The seeded extension 23 seconds ago' plus every file), and screen 05 renders. GITHUB IMPORT: 'Import a repo instead' on screen 02 opens the import wizard without leaving the page, and the workspace's publish split menu still carries 'Import from GitHub' beside 'Publish to GitHub' and 'Remove local install'. PUBLISH: both reachable publishes work and are described correctly - the dialog's 'Load into this Rancher' and 'Push the source to GitHub' rows are tickable and marked 'No sign-off'. SETTINGS: /barn/settings carries all of it (What needs sign-off, GitHub connection, What the assistant may do without asking, Where previews run, Who can use Studio, What is sent to the model). The two regressions: (1) the hand-over no longer refuses without a brief - assemblePacket()'s brief check is gone and the record/PR body say plainly when there is none, so 'Push the source to GitHub' works on a brief-less extension again; (2) a refused hand-over no longer moves HEAD - I ticked 'Push the source to GitHub' on w3rc with no token configured and let it refuse, and `git rev-parse HEAD` in the pod read 6cbb9a4968ab26c4be26dd208c62d21d7c172877 both before and after, with the working tree untouched. The dialog copy that used to describe the removed behaviour is also corrected: it now reads 'assembles the work into a packet, pushes that packet to a branch of its own (barn/w3rc/3) in that repository, and opens a pull request against the default branch. Nothing is merged and nothing is written to main.'
